name: Core
signature: class Core : OnMapDownloadedObservable, OnMapUpdateAvailableObservable, OnMapDownloadErrorObservable, OnMapExtractionProgressObservable, OnMapDownloadProgressObservable, OnInitProgressObservable, OnHybridDownloadProgressObservable, OnCoreInitObservable, OnLicenseErrorObservable, OnOfflinePeriodExpiredObservable
summary: Entry point of the MSDK: initialises the native core, the license and the maps that the other modules use.
doc:
Entry point of the MSDK: initialises the native core, the license and the maps that the other modules use.

Use the single instance returned by `getInstance`; never create one with the constructor. Call `init` once, then wait for `OnCoreInitCallback.onCoreReady` before using any other module that depends on the Core. Every callback and observer is called on the main thread. Add and remove observers on the main thread too.

name: cancelPendingHybridDownloads
summary: This method cancels any pending map download operations when working with hybrid maps.
doc:
This method cancels any pending map download operations when working with hybrid maps.

It also pauses hybrid map downloads for 3 seconds: map download requests made during that time are discarded, without any notification. It does nothing when `isUsingHybridMaps` returns false.

name: downloadAvailableUpdate
summary: Answers a map update offer: starts the download of the update, or declines it.
doc:
Answers a map update offer: starts the download of the update, or declines it.

Only call this method after `OnMapUpdateAvailableCallback.onMapUpdateAvailable` is triggered (use `addOnMapUpdateAvailableObserver`). To get the download progress of the update, subscribe to `OnMapDownloadProgressCallback` (use `addOnMapDownloadProgressObserver`). You can also be notified when the download has finished by subscribing to `OnMapDownloadedCallback` (use `addOnMapDownloadedObserver`).

The downloaded update will be installed on the next app launch.

params.name: downloadAccepted
params.doc: true to download the update; false to decline it, which also stops it from being offered again until the app restarts.

id: com.benomad.msdk.core.Core.init(Context, String?, String?, String, String?, String?, OnCoreInitCallback)
name: init
signature: fun init(applicationContext: Context, purchaseUUID: String?, licenseKey: String? = null, mapsDeploymentPath: String = getDefaultMapsPath(applicationContext), resourcesPathInAssets: String? = ResourcesHandler.defaultAssetsResourcesFolderName, mapsPathInAssets: String? = ResourcesHandler.defaultAssetMapsFolderName, callback: OnCoreInitCallback)
summary: Starts the initialisation of the Core and returns immediately.
doc:
Starts the initialisation of the Core and returns immediately.

The initialisation is mandatory before using any module that depends on the Core. It runs in the background: it deploys the resources and maps bundled in the assets, activates the license, then loads the maps. The outcome is delivered on the main thread, to `callback` and to every observer added with `addOnCoreInitObserver`: `OnCoreInitCallback.onCoreReady` on success, `OnCoreInitCallback.onCoreInitError` or `OnCoreInitCallback.onCoreInitException` on failure.

Call it once per process: check `isInit` first, and never call it again after `OnCoreInitCallback.onCoreReady`. A call made while an initialisation is running fails with `CoreErrorCodes.BUSY`; observers can receive that error too, and it says nothing about the running initialisation. To retry after `OnCoreInitCallback.onCoreInitError`, post the new call to the main thread from an observer added with `addOnCoreInitObserver`, or make it on a later user action; never call `init` directly from inside a callback. If a retry fails with `CoreErrorCodes.BUSY` while none of your calls is waiting for its outcome, the Core can't be initialised again in this process.

Progress: `OnInitProgressCallback` (see `addOnInitProgressObserver`) reports the loading of the maps, the last step. Map downloads and extractions report through `addOnMapDownloadProgressObserver` and `addOnMapExtractionProgressObserver`. Add the observers before calling `init`.

Requirements:

- the app declares the INTERNET permission; the MSDK manifests do not declare it;
- the first initialisation needs an Internet connection, to activate the license;
- on Android 7 to 9 (API 24 to 28), the initialisation reads the device IMEI, so the READ_PHONE_STATE permission must be granted before calling `init`.

params.name: applicationContext
params.doc: the application context

params.name: purchaseUUID
params.doc: the BeNomad purchase UUID of your order. Required.

params.name: licenseKey
params.doc: (Optional) Forces activation with this license key. If the key is not available, `init` fails and an error is returned.

params.name: mapsDeploymentPath
params.doc: absolute path of the folder that holds the maps; defaults to `getDefaultMapsPath`. The Core owns this folder: when the maps bundled in `mapsPathInAssets` change version, `init` deletes everything in it before copying them. Never use a folder that holds other files.

params.name: resourcesPathInAssets
params.doc: path, relative to the app's assets, of the resources folder to deploy; defaults to `"benomad_resources"` (`getDefaultAssetsResourcesPath`). Pass null if the app ships no resources: if the folder is missing from the assets, `init` can fail with `CoreErrorCodes.NO_RESOURCES_IN_ASSETS`.

params.name: mapsPathInAssets
params.doc: path, relative to the app's assets, of the maps folder bundled with the app; defaults to `"Maps"` (`getDefaultAssetsMapsPath`). Bundled maps are optional: pass null if the app ships none.

params.name: callback
params.doc: receives the outcome. Other observers can be added with `addOnCoreInitObserver`.

summary: After receiving the OnCoreReady notification, this method returns true while the loaded maps still contain at least one partial (hybrid) file, whose full maps are downloaded when needed.

`cancelPendingHybridDownloads`, `loadFullMapsInArea` and `loadFullMapsInCountry` only act while it returns true.

name: loadFullMapsInArea
signature: fun loadFullMapsInArea(area: GeoRect, asyncMode: Boolean = false): Error?
summary: After receiving the OnCoreReady notification (and if you are using hybrid maps), you can use this method to force the download of full maps within a given area (if area's maps has partial files).
doc:
After receiving the OnCoreReady notification (and if you are using hybrid maps), you can use this method to force the download of full maps within a given area (if area's maps has partial files).

In synchronous mode (the default), the call blocks until the download ends: never call it on the main thread. In asynchronous mode, it returns at once.

params.name: area
params.doc: the rectangular area to download.

params.name: asyncMode
params.doc: true to start the download and return at once; false (default) to block until the download ends.

returns: an error if the Core is not initialised (`CoreErrorCodes.CORE_NOT_YET_INITIALIZED`) or if the maps are not hybrid (`CoreErrorCodes.CORE_NOT_USING_HYBRID_MAPS`); null otherwise. A null result means that the download was requested, not that it succeeded.

name: loadFullMapsInCountry

summary: After receiving the OnCoreReady notification (and if you are using hybrid maps), you can use this method to force the download of full maps within a given country (if country's maps has partial files).
doc:
After receiving the OnCoreReady notification (and if you are using hybrid maps), you can use this method to force the download of full maps within a given country (if country's maps has partial files).

In synchronous mode (the default), the call blocks until the download ends: never call it on the main thread. In asynchronous mode, it returns at once.

params.name: countryCode
params.doc: The ISO 3166 Alpha-3 code of the country to download

params.name: asyncMode
params.doc: true to start the download and return at once; false (default) to block until the download ends.

returns: an error if the Core is not initialised (`CoreErrorCodes.CORE_NOT_YET_INITIALIZED`) or if the maps are not hybrid (`CoreErrorCodes.CORE_NOT_USING_HYBRID_MAPS`); null otherwise. A null result means that the download was requested, not that it succeeded.

throws.label: IllegalArgumentException
throws.doc: if `countryCode` is not 3 characters long.

Class ID for highlighted objects.

Class IDs are unsigned 32-bit values, and this one, 0xFFFFFF00, does not fit in a positive `int`: this constant reads as -256, and so does its `toLong()`. Class IDs read from the maps as a `long` are positive, so compare them with `Integer.toUnsignedLong(KB_HIGHLIGHT_CLASS)` (4294967040).

name: LanguageCode
summary: Languages of the names stored in the maps, with a few special codes.
doc:
Languages of the names stored in the maps, with a few special codes.

`value` is the map attribute code of the names in the language: one of the `KB_ATT_*` codes of `CartoConst`. Four entries are special codes rather than languages: `DEFAULT_LANGUAGE` (the official name, attribute code "ON"), `ANY_LANGUAGE` (all languages, "XX"), `COUNTRY_CODE` (the ISO 3166 alpha-3 country code, "IC") and `OFFICIAL_CODE` ("OC").

The list is not complete: the maps can hold names in languages that have no entry here.

`isoCode2`, `isoCode3` and `isoCode3Alt` are BeNomad codes. For most languages they are the ISO 639-1, ISO 639-3 and ISO 639-2/B codes, but not for all:

- some two-letter codes are not ISO 639-1 codes, or are the ISO 639-1 code of another language: "bi" is Bengali here (Bislama in ISO 639-1), "ka" is Kannada (Georgian), "kl" is Kazakh in the latin alphabet (Greenlandic), "ht" is Hindi in the latin alphabet (Haitian) and "ae" is Arabic-English (Avestan). "el" is Greek in the latin alphabet; Greek in the greek alphabet is "eg";
- the ISO 639-1 codes "bn" (Bengali), "kn" (Kannada), "ml" (Malayalam) and "id" (Indonesian) have no entry;
- some three-letter codes are the ISO 639-3 code of another language, for example "kal", "hil", "are", "chl", "the", "ukl", "gai", "gdh", "axm", "bet", "bex", "bun", "kol", "kxn", "mat" and "scl"; so are some alternative codes, such as "gag" (Galician here, Gagauz in ISO 639-3). The ISO 639-3 codes "gle" (Irish) and "gla" (Scottish Gaelic) have no entry.

So `valueOfIsoCode2` and `valueOfIsoCode3` can return another language than the one an ISO code names, or null: check the result. A `java.util.Locale` can also give codes that this table does not use: on Android, `Locale.getLanguage()` returns "iw" for Hebrew, which is "he" here.

name: BUSY
summary: This call to `Core.init` was refused and started nothing, for example because an initialisation is running.
doc:
This call to `Core.init` was refused and started nothing, for example because an initialisation is running. Reported with `ErrorType.CORE` to the callback of that call; the observers added with `Core.addOnCoreInitObserver` can receive it too. It does not report the outcome of any other call: rely on the outcome of the call that started the initialisation, and on `Core.isInit`.

The native layer also reports code 18, with an empty messageId, when the road network cannot be built from the maps: compare the `messageId` to tell the two apart.

name: CORE_NOT_USING_HYBRID_MAPS
summary: The loaded maps are not hybrid (`Core.isUsingHybridMaps` returns false).
doc: The loaded maps are not hybrid (`Core.isUsingHybridMaps` returns false). Returned with `ErrorType.CORE` by `Core.loadFullMapsInArea` and `Core.loadFullMapsInCountry`.

name: CORE_NOT_YET_INITIALIZED
doc: The Core is not initialised. Returned with `ErrorType.CORE` by `Core.loadFullMapsInArea` and `Core.loadFullMapsInCountry`.

name: EXTERNAL_STORAGE_NOT_ACCESSIBLE
summary: The external storage of the device is not readable or writable.
doc: The external storage of the device is not readable or writable. Reported with `ErrorType.CORE_RESOURCES` by `Core.init`, until a first initialisation has succeeded.

name: FUNCTION_NOT_ALLOWED
summary: The license does not allow the requested function, for example the circuit functions of the Navigation and Geocoder modules (`CircuitNavigation.startSession`, `GeoDecoder.mapMatchCircuitWaypoints`).
doc: The license does not allow the requested function, for example the circuit functions of the Navigation and Geocoder modules (`CircuitNavigation.startSession`, `GeoDecoder.mapMatchCircuitWaypoints`). Reported with `ErrorType.CORE`.

name: INCOMPLETE_VERSIONING_FILE
summary: The versioning file lacks some of its fields.
doc: The versioning file lacks some of its fields. Reported like `NOT_READABLE_FILE`.

name: MAPS_UPDATE_FAILED
summary: The maps bundled in the app's assets changed version, and `Core.init` could not delete the previous maps from the maps folder (`mapsDeploymentPath`), so they were not replaced.
doc: The maps bundled in the app's assets changed version, and `Core.init` could not delete the previous maps from the maps folder (`mapsDeploymentPath`), so they were not replaced. Reported with `ErrorType.CORE_RESOURCES`.

name: NOT_READABLE_FILE
summary: The versioning file, which the Core keeps in the app's internal storage, is not readable.
doc: The versioning file, which the Core keeps in the app's internal storage, is not readable. Reported with `ErrorType.CORE_RESOURCES`: `Core.init` can report it when it rewrites that file.

doc: The report file of `ReportingManager` is not readable. Reported with `ErrorType.CORE`.

doc: The versioning file is not writable. Reported like `NOT_READABLE_FILE`.

Its position (`getGeoPoint`, `x`, `y`) is in WGS84 decimal degrees: x is the longitude and y the latitude.

name: GeoWaypoint
summary: A class that defines a Waypoint.
doc:
A class that defines a Waypoint. A Waypoint is similar to a via-point plus a radius which defines the distance under which the routing algorithm considers that the via-point is reached. Note that waypoints with a radius >0 are also known as "soft waypoints". If this location is an intermediate point passed to the route planner, `getAvoidUTurn` defines if route planner must avoid (if possible) a U-turn after reaching waypoint's location. If this location is not the last point passed to the route planner, `isIgnoreTrafficDirections` defines if route planner can ignore traffic directions to reach following point passed to the planner (allowing going against traffic directions).

To get the position of a waypoint, read the coordinates of the `Waypoint`, or of the `com.benomad.msdk.core.svs.GeoPoint`, whose road location it is, rather than `getGeoPoint`, `x` or `y`. For a GeoWaypoint that you build yourself, keep the position of the point you built it from.

The public constructors need the Core's native library: create waypoints only after `Core.getInstance()` has been called, for example once the Core is initialised.

signature: open class Waypoint(lon: Double, lat: Double, val heading: Double = Double.NaN, val transportationMode: TranspMode = TranspMode.PASSENGER_CAR, val radius: Int = 0, var alertRadius: Int = 50, val avoidUTurn: WaypointStatus = WaypointStatus.UNDEF, var useStartAngle: WaypointStatus = WaypointStatus.UNDEF, val useStopRoadSide: WaypointStatus = WaypointStatus.UNDEF, val ignoreTrafficDirection: Boolean = false, val ignoreRoadBlocks: Boolean = false, val ignoreRestrictions: Boolean = false, val ignorePoint: Boolean = false, val ignoreVehicleProfile: Boolean = false, val stopTime: Int = 0, val maxDrivingSpeed: Int = 0, val offroadPolyline: List<GeoPoint>? = null) : GeoPoint
summary: Defines a Waypoint which is a `GeoPoint` plus additional properties that can impact the routing algorithm.
doc:
Defines a Waypoint which is a `GeoPoint` plus additional properties that can impact the routing algorithm. For instance, the radius which defines the distance under which the routing algorithm considers that the waypoint is reached.

If this location is an intermediate point passed to the route planner, `avoidUTurn` defines if route planner must avoid (if possible) a U-turn after reaching waypoint's location. If this location is not the last waypoint passed to the route planner, `ignoreTrafficDirection` defines if route planner can ignore traffic directions to reach following waypoint passed to the planner (allowing going against traffic directions).

A waypoint built by `create` has a road location (`roadLocation`), which is a `GeoWaypoint`. To get the position of the waypoint, read its own longitude and latitude, never the coordinates of its road location.

name: create
summary: Creates a `Waypoint` from a map-matched `GeoPoint`: a point whose road location (`point.roadLocation`) is set, such as the position of a geocoded address.
doc:
Creates a `Waypoint` from a map-matched `GeoPoint`: a point whose road location (`point.roadLocation`) is set, such as the position of a geocoded address.

The waypoint is placed on the road: its longitude and latitude are the position where `point` was matched, not `point`'s own coordinates, and its `Waypoint.heading` is the angle of the road segment. When the road location is a `GeoWaypoint`, the new waypoint takes its settings (radius, statuses...). Its `Waypoint.alertRadius` is at least its `Waypoint.radius`, and its `Waypoint.offroadPolyline` is null.

params.name: point
params.doc: a map-matched point

returns: a new `Waypoint`, or null if `point` has no road location or if the waypoint cannot be created.

name: CoordIterator
summary: Provides a generic iterator for traversing geometric coordinates of any SVS Form (except an `AbstractForm`).
doc:
Provides a generic iterator for traversing geometric coordinates of any SVS Form (except an `AbstractForm`).

Call `hasMoreElements` exactly once before each call to `nextElement`: `hasMoreElements` reads the next point, and `nextElement` returns the point it read. Coordinates are in decimal degrees: x is the longitude, y the latitude. Use the iterator only once the Core is initialised.

A polyline or a polygon yields its points in order. A rectangle or an ellipse yields two points: the min corner, then the max corner of its rectangle. A point form yields one point: its first point, whatever the index.

name: DynamicLayersGroup
summary: This class provides methods for creating a group of additional layers in which geometric forms such as points, lines, polylines, polygons, etc. can be added and removed dynamically.
doc:
This class provides methods for creating a group of additional layers in which geometric forms such as points, lines, polylines, polygons, etc. can be added and removed dynamically. To draw the group, attach it to a map with `MapView.attachDynamicLayers` (Mapping module).

Create the group, and add forms to it, only once the Core is initialised (after `onCoreReady`). Coordinates are `GeoPoint`s in decimal degrees.

Forms and ownership: the forms returned by the `new` methods, and the forms inserted with `addForm`, belong to the group. A form belongs to one group, and to one class, at a time; `remove(classID, form, detach)` takes it out of the group and gives it back to the caller. A form of the group stays valid only while the group is alive: keep a reference to the group as long as you use its forms.

Note about the class identifier (classID):

The maps already define cartographic class IDs; `CartoConst` lists most of them. You can use one of them for a new layer: the layer is then rendered with the style defined for that class ID. You can also use your own class ID. It must not be a class ID of the maps: by convention, custom class IDs are between 12000 and 12999, a range that no class of the maps uses; this class does not check the range. A layer is drawn only if a style exists for its class ID: a style of the map style sheets, or a style created with `createPOIStyle`, `createPolylineStyle` or `createPolygonStyle` of `MapStyle` (Mapping module).

The z-index of the layers is defined by their class ID: a higher class ID means a higher z-index. For example, a layer with a classID of 10003L will be rendered on top of all layers with a classID < 10003L.

name: addForm

summary: Inserts the given SVS `form` in the layer that corresponds to the specified `classID`.
doc:
Inserts the given SVS `form` in the layer that corresponds to the specified `classID`. On success, the group takes ownership of the form.

Note: a `Form` can be added to only one `DynamicLayersGroup`, and to one class, at a time: a form that already belongs to a group, such as a form returned by a `new` method, is refused. To add a `Form` to another class or another `DynamicLayersGroup`, you have to remove it first from the one it is attached to, using `remove(classID, form, detach)`.

params.name: atts

```kotlin

        already has.
```

returns: false if an error occurs and the `form` couldn't be added, true otherwise.

Warning: all `Form` that were added to the layer that corresponds to the `classID` will be destroyed, including the forms inserted with `addForm`. Don't use these `Form` objects afterwards, even when another object still references them (for example the polyline of a route inserted with `addForm`). To keep a form, take it out of the layer first, using `remove(classID, form, detach)`.

Represents a geographical 2D rectangular area defined by two opposite corners, in decimal degrees: the min corner (x = minimum longitude, y = minimum latitude) and the max corner (x = maximum longitude, y = maximum latitude).

Always pass the minimum longitude and latitude as the min corner, and the maximum ones as the max corner: `contains`, `intersectsWith` and `intersects` rely on it.

Internal identifier of a geographical element, such as an object clicked on the map. Use it with `create` to get the element's forms, or `getClassId` to get its class.

name: GestureOptions
summary: Class used to enable or disable gestures of a `MapView`.
doc:
Class used to enable or disable gestures of a `MapView`. By default, every gesture is enabled.

- `Gesture.PAN`: moving the map with one or two fingers.
- `Gesture.PINCH`: zooming with two fingers.
- `Gesture.ROTATE`: rotating the map with two fingers.
- `Gesture.TILT`: tilting the map by moving two fingers up or down together.
- `Gesture.DOUBLE_TAP`: zooming in with a double tap (see `MapView.doubleTapZoomScale`).

To turn the click results of taps and long presses on or off, use the `tap` and `longPress` parameters of `MapView.setMapClickedListener`.

To change the gestures of a view, change the options it uses (`MapView.gestureOptions`) with `setGestureStatus`, `disableAllGestures` or `enableAllGestures`, rather than assigning new `GestureOptions` to it.

name: MapView
signature: open class MapView @JvmOverloads constructor(context: Context, attrs: AttributeSet? = null, gestureOptions: GestureOptions = GestureOptions(), onGestureListener: OnGestureListener? = null, onStateChanged: suspend (newState: MapState) -> Unit = {}, callback: OnMapReadyCallback? = null) : GLMapView, TwoFingersGestureDetector.OnTwoFingersGestureListener
summary: An interactive map, shown as an Android view.
doc:
An interactive map, shown as an Android view.

The `MapView` can be manipulated only after `OnMapReadyCallback.onMapReady` is called. Before that, only set its listeners and options (such as `gestureOptions` or `maxTiltAngle`), add observers with `addOnMapReadyObserver`, and call `setMapStyle`, whose style is applied once the map is created. After the view is destroyed, don't call its methods. Until the map is ready, and after the view is destroyed, the values read from the map are 0, false or null (`center` is (0, 0)).

Lifecycle:

- Create the view on the main thread. Its native map is created once the Core is initialized and the view is attached to a window, visible and laid out; `OnMapReadyCallback.onMapReady` is then called on the main thread.
- Destroy the view when it is no longer needed: call `onDestroy` on the main thread, or register the view as an observer of the lifecycle it belongs to (`lifecycle.addObserver(mapView)`; in a fragment, use `viewLifecycleOwner.lifecycle`). Until then, the view, its context and its native map stay in memory. A destroyed view can't be used again: build a new one.
- Don't call the `onPause()` and `onResume()` methods that the view inherits from `GLSurfaceView`: the view manages its rendering itself.
- Don't move the view to another parent, and don't remove it from its window to add it back later: to show the map elsewhere, destroy the view and build a new one.
- If the Navigation module uses this map, stop the guidance session before destroying the view.

The view saves its `MapState` with its instance state when its map is ready, and the view that restores this instance state re-applies it once its own map is ready. Android saves the instance state of a view only when the view has an id.

params.name: context
params.doc: the context of the activity or fragment that shows the view. The view keeps it until it is destroyed.

params.name: attrs
params.doc: the XML attributes of the view, when it is inflated from a layout; null otherwise.

params.name: gestureOptions
params.doc: used to define the gestures status (enabled or disabled). By default, all gestures are enabled if nothing is passed for this optional argument.

params.name: onGestureListener
params.doc: used to be notified about gestures performed on the `MapView` (optional).

params.name: onStateChanged
params.doc: called with the new `MapState` when the camera of the map changes, on a background thread, at most about once every 200 ms. It can skip states, including the last one of a gesture or of the inertia: to know where the camera stopped, call `getCurrentMapState` on the main thread. Each call runs in its own coroutine, so a call can start before the previous one has returned. It can only be set here.

params.name: callback
params.doc: the `OnMapReadyCallback` to be notified when the map is ready to be manipulated, or if the map initialization encountered an error (see `addOnMapReadyObserver`). When the map becomes ready, the view also sets it up: it re-applies a saved `MapState`, if any, and enables inertia (500 ms, see `enableInertia`). To change the camera or the inertia at that time, do it in an observer added with `addOnMapReadyObserver` once the view is built: it is notified after that set-up. From Java, reaching this parameter means passing `onStateChanged`, a suspending function: add the callback with `addOnMapReadyObserver` instead.

id: com.benomad.msdk.mapping.MapView.MapView(Context, AttributeSet?, GestureOptions, OnGestureListener?, suspend (newState: MapState) -> Unit, OnMapReadyCallback?)
name: MapView
signature: @JvmOverloadsconstructor(context: Context, attrs: AttributeSet? = null, gestureOptions: GestureOptions = GestureOptions(), onGestureListener: OnGestureListener? = null, onStateChanged: suspend (newState: MapState) -> Unit = {}, callback: OnMapReadyCallback? = null)
doc: Creates a map view. Create it on the main thread.

params.name: context
params.doc: the context of the activity or fragment that shows the view. The view keeps it until it is destroyed.

params.name: attrs
params.doc: the XML attributes of the view, when it is inflated from a layout; null otherwise.

params.name: gestureOptions
params.doc: used to define the gestures status (enabled or disabled). By default, all gestures are enabled if nothing is passed for this optional argument.

params.name: onGestureListener
params.doc: used to be notified about gestures performed on the `MapView` (optional).

params.name: onStateChanged
params.doc: called with the new `MapState` when the camera of the map changes, on a background thread, at most about once every 200 ms. It can skip states, including the last one of a gesture or of the inertia: to know where the camera stopped, call `getCurrentMapState` on the main thread. Each call runs in its own coroutine, so a call can start before the previous one has returned. It can only be set here.

params.name: callback
params.doc: the `OnMapReadyCallback` to be notified when the map is ready to be manipulated, or if the map initialization encountered an error (see `addOnMapReadyObserver`). When the map becomes ready, the view also sets it up: it re-applies a saved `MapState`, if any, and enables inertia (500 ms, see `enableInertia`). To change the camera or the inertia at that time, do it in an observer added with `addOnMapReadyObserver` once the view is built: it is notified after that set-up. From Java, reaching this parameter means passing `onStateChanged`, a suspending function: add the callback with `addOnMapReadyObserver` instead.

name: attachDynamicLayers
summary: Attach a group of dynamic layer(s) to this Map View.
doc:
Attach a group of dynamic layer(s) to this Map View. All geometric objects/layers will be rendered according to the current `MapStyle`

Attach the group once the map is ready (`OnMapReadyCallback.onMapReady`), and keep the view in its window afterwards (see the class description). Attach one group at a time: to show another group, detach the current one with `detachDynamicLayers` first.
returns: true if the group has been attached, false if it is already attached to this view or could not be attached

name: center
summary: Returns the current 2D-center point of the view.
doc: Returns the current 2D-center point of the view.
returns: a `GeoPoint` that corresponds to the 2D-center point of the view, or (0, 0) until the map is ready.

name: setProjParameters
signature: fun setProjParameters(rotationAngle: Double, tiltAngle: Double, inZoomLevel: Double, point: GeoPoint, pt1: Point, pt2: Point, redraw: Boolean): Boolean
summary: Sets new projection parameters: this is equivalent to, but faster than, successive calls to methods `rotate`, `tilt`, `zoomTo` and `move`.
doc:
Sets new projection parameters: this is equivalent to, but faster than, successive calls to methods `rotate`, `tilt`, `zoomTo` and `move`.

Unlike `tilt`, `zoom` and `zoomTo`, it does not limit `tiltAngle` to `maxTiltAngle`, nor `inZoomLevel` to the range from `minZoomLevel` to `maxZoomLevel`: pass values within those limits. It does not notify the `onCenterChangeListener` either.

params.name: rotationAngle
params.doc: Rotation angle around z axis in degrees.

params.name: tiltAngle
params.doc: Rotation angle around x axis in degrees.

params.name: inZoomLevel
params.doc: the new zoom level (see `zoomLevel`).

params.name: point
params.doc: the point to center the view on, before the move.

params.name: pt1
params.doc: the start, in pixels, of the screen vector by which the view is then moved (see `move`).

params.name: pt2
params.doc: the end, in pixels, of that vector. Pass the same point as `pt1` for no move.

params.name: redraw
params.doc: A flag that indicates whether the view must be redrawn or not.

returns: true on success, false otherwise (for example before the map is ready).

name: setViewType
summary: Updates the view type of the `MapView`, then redraws the map.
doc:
Updates the view type of the `MapView`, then redraws the map.

Can only be used after the `OnMapReadyCallback.onMapReady` is triggered: before that, the call does nothing.

- `ViewType.TWO_DIMENSIONS_ORIENTED_NORTH` sets the tilt and the rotation to 0.
- `ViewType.TWO_DIMENSIONS` sets the tilt to 0.
- `ViewType.THREE_DIMENSIONS` tilts the map to a default angle when it is not tilted.
- `ViewType.AUTO` changes neither the tilt nor the rotation.

The view type is also saved in a setting that all the maps of the app share.

name: showRoadRestrictions
signature: fun showRoadRestrictions(roadRestrictions: Boolean = true, roadRestrictionsPOI: Boolean = true, profile: Profile? = null)
summary: Show or hide display of the road restrictions of a vehicle profile.
doc:
Show or hide display of the road restrictions of a vehicle profile.

The restrictions are shown only for a `profile`: when `profile` is null, the default, they are hidden whatever `roadRestrictions` and `roadRestrictionsPOI` say. So a call with no argument hides them.

params.name: roadRestrictions
params.doc: display road restrictions.

params.name: roadRestrictionsPOI
params.doc: display POI of restrictions (needs `roadRestrictions` parameter to be enabled).

params.name: profile
params.doc: vehicle profile to show road restriction on map or null to hide them.

since: v2.8.0 Renamed parameter `show` to `roadRestrictions`, added `roadRestrictionsPOI` and `profile` parameters.

name: tilt
summary: Sets a rotation angle around x axis (the tilt).
doc:
Sets a rotation angle around x axis (the tilt).

The map x angle is bounded by 0 and `maxTiltAngle` (65° by default), which means that if `angle`< 0, the map x angle will be set to 0 and if `angle`>`maxTiltAngle`, the map x angle will be set to `maxTiltAngle`. The map never tilts more than 80°, whatever `maxTiltAngle`.

params.name: angle
params.doc: the rotation angle around x axis in degrees.

params.name: redraw
params.doc: A flag that indicates whether the view must be redrawn or not.

name: tiltAngle
returns: The current tilt angle in degrees, or 0 until the map is ready.

summary: Updates map orientation to 2D north (tilt and orientation set to 0)
doc: Updates map orientation to 2D north (tilt and orientation set to 0)

name: updateMapState
doc:
Updates the `MapView` with a new `MapState`. Call it once the map is ready.

When only the zoom level differs from the current state, the change is animated: the zoom level moves by steps of `doubleTapZoomScaleStep` (see `zoomIn` and `zoomOut`), and the call returns after the last step, which can pass the requested zoom level by up to one step. Otherwise the new state is applied at once. To set an exact zoom level without animation, use `zoom`.

params.name: mapState
params.doc: the new `MapState`

doc: Returns the height of the view (in pixels).

doc: Returns the width of the view (in pixels).
returns: The width of the view (in pixels), or 0 until the map is ready.

name: zoom
summary: Performs a zoom operation centered on the view
doc: Performs a zoom operation centered on the view

params.name: inZoomLevel
params.doc: the new zoom level (see `zoomLevel`). It is limited to the range from `minZoomLevel` to `maxZoomLevel`.

params.name: inRedraw
params.doc: A flag that indicates whether the view must be redrawn or not.

name: zoomIn
summary: Zooms in with an animation, centered on the view: the zoom level grows by steps of `doubleTapZoomScaleStep`, which must be greater than 0, and the map is redrawn at each step.
doc: Zooms in with an animation, centered on the view: the zoom level grows by steps of `doubleTapZoomScaleStep`, which must be greater than 0, and the map is redrawn at each step. The call returns after the last step. It does nothing if the zoom level is already `inZoomLevel` or higher. To set an exact zoom level without animation, use `zoom`.

params.name: inZoomLevel
params.doc: the zoom level to zoom in to, at most `maxZoomLevel` (see `zoomLevel`). The last step can pass it, by up to `doubleTapZoomScaleStep`: to end exactly on it, call `zoom` with it afterwards.

name: zoomLevel
summary: Returns the current zoom level, or 0 until the map is ready.
doc:
Returns the current zoom level, or 0 until the map is ready.

Zoom level 0 is the zoom level where the whole Earth, from the South to the North pole, is visible, whatever the screen's size and density and the map data. Zoom level n = twice the scale of zoom level n-1. In other words the number of meters per pixel at zoom level n is half the number of meters at zoom level n-1.

summary: Zooms out with an animation, centered on the view: the zoom level decreases by steps of `doubleTapZoomScaleStep`, which must be greater than 0, and the map is redrawn at each step.

The call returns after the last step. It does nothing if the zoom level is already `inZoomLevel` or lower. To set an exact zoom level without animation, use `zoom`.

params.doc: the zoom level to zoom out to, at least `minZoomLevel` (see `zoomLevel`). The last step can pass it, by up to `doubleTapZoomScaleStep`: to end exactly on it, call `zoom` with it afterwards.

summary: Notifies when the `MapView` initialization fails: the view could not create its map.
doc:
Notifies when the `MapView` initialization fails: the view could not create its map. Called on the main thread.

After a failure, each later change of the view's surface retries the creation: the error can be reported again, and `onMapReady` can follow it. A failure of the Core initialization is not reported here but by the Core's own callbacks; the map only becomes ready once the Core is initialized.

name: onMapReady
summary: Notifies when the `MapView` initialization is done and can be manipulated.
doc:
Notifies when the `MapView` initialization is done and can be manipulated. Called on the main thread.

It is delivered once per creation of the view's native map, which only happens once the Core is initialized and the view's surface has been sized (the view is attached to a window, visible and laid out). A view that never gets a sized surface, e.g. one that is never attached, therefore never becomes ready.

name: onCenterChanged
summary: Called on the main thread when a pan gesture starts, just before the map moves.
doc:
Called on the main thread when a pan gesture starts, just before the map moves.

It can also be called when a zoom moves the center: a pinch, a double tap, or a call to `MapView.zoomTo` or `MapView.zoomToRect`, then on the thread that made the call.

It is not called for the rest of a pan, for the inertia that follows it, for `MapView.move` or `MapView.setProjParameters`, nor for the camera moves made by navigation. Read `MapView.center` to get the current center.

Interface that defines callbacks for listening `MapView` clicks.

Register it with `MapView.setMapClickedListener`, which also turns the taps and the long presses on: they are off by default. After an enabled tap or long press, the view searches the map at that point in the background, then calls the listener on the main thread with what it found (see `MapClickedResults`).

name: MapClickedResults
signature: data class MapClickedResults(val addresses: List<Address>?, val clusters: List<ClusterResult>?, val objects: List<ClickedObject>?)
summary: Results returned when the map is clicked or long-pressed (see `com.benomad.msdk.mapping.callbacks.OnMapClickedListener`).
doc:
Results returned when the map is clicked or long-pressed (see `com.benomad.msdk.mapping.callbacks.OnMapClickedListener`).

When the search at the clicked location could run, `addresses` is never null, while `clusters` and `objects` are null when nothing of their kind was found. When the search could not run (another search was running, the map or the Core was not ready, or the search failed), all three are null. So check `addresses` for null to tell a search that did not run from a search that found nothing.

name: MapStyle
summary: A Map Style lets you configure how vector maps have to be rendered in a `com.benomad.msdk.mapping.MapView`.
doc:
A Map Style lets you configure how vector maps have to be rendered in a `com.benomad.msdk.mapping.MapView`.

Get a map style from `MapStyleLoader`: load it with `MapStyleLoader.loadStyle`, get it with `MapStyleLoader.getStyle`, then apply it with `com.benomad.msdk.mapping.MapView.setMapStyle`. Never create one with the constructor: such a style holds no graphic chart, and its methods must not be called.

Call the methods of a map style on the main thread: they are not synchronized.

name: getMapDataPOIClassIDs
signature: @JvmStatic@JvmOverloadsfun getMapDataPOIClassIDs(minClassID: Long = CartoConst.KB_VEHICLE_REPAIR.toLong(), maxClassID: Long = CartoConst.KB_TRUCK_REPAIR_AND_SERVICE.toLong()): LongArray
summary: Returns the POI classes found in the installed map files, sorted by ascending class ID.
doc:
Returns the POI classes found in the installed map files, sorted by ascending class ID.

A class is listed if its ID is between `minClassID` and `maxClassID` (both included), if it is a POI class of the address search (so the city centres, 7379, and hamlets, 7381, are never listed), and if the installed map files contain POIs of this class. Dynamic data (traffic, dynamic POIs, route highlight, external layers) is not read.

No map style is read, so unlike the `MapStyle` methods this one can be called from any thread. Scanning the map files takes tens of milliseconds on a phone, so call it off the main thread. Then keep the categories of `getPOICategories` (a map style lookup, main thread) whose class ID it returns: this lists the POI categories of the installed maps without blocking the main thread.

params.name: minClassID
params.doc: the lowest class ID to list (default `CartoConst.KB_VEHICLE_REPAIR`, 7310).

params.name: maxClassID
params.doc: the highest class ID to list (default `CartoConst.KB_TRUCK_REPAIR_AND_SERVICE`, 9958).

returns: the POI class IDs, or an empty array if the Core is not initialized, if the licence is locked or expired, or if the range is invalid.

name: getPOICategories
signature: @JvmOverloadsfun getPOICategories(minClassID: Long = CartoConst.KB_VEHICLE_REPAIR.toLong(), maxClassID: Long = CartoConst.KB_TRUCK_REPAIR_AND_SERVICE.toLong()): List<POICategory>
summary: Returns the POI categories of this map style, sorted by ascending class ID.
doc:
Returns the POI categories of this map style, sorted by ascending class ID.

A class is listed if:

- its ID is between `minClassID` and `maxClassID` (both included);
- it is a POI class of the address search, so the city centres (7379) and hamlets (7381) are never listed;
- this map style draws its points with an image (`POICategory.iconPath`).

Only the map style is read, so the list does not depend on the Core, the licence or the installed maps. Every class ID of the range is checked, so keep the range narrow: a range wider than 65536 class IDs is refused (empty list), because it would block the main thread. To list only the categories present in the installed map files, call `getMapDataPOIClassIDs` off the main thread and keep the categories of this list whose class ID it returns.

This method must be called on the main thread, where the map styles are created and deleted: map style lookups are not synchronized.

params.name: minClassID
params.doc: the lowest class ID to list (default `CartoConst.KB_VEHICLE_REPAIR`, 7310).

params.name: maxClassID
params.doc: the highest class ID to list (default `CartoConst.KB_TRUCK_REPAIR_AND_SERVICE`, 9958).

returns: the POI categories, or an empty list if none is found.

summary: Shows or hides several classes at once.
doc:
Shows or hides several classes at once.

Unknown classes and classes already in the requested state are ignored. The maps using this style are invalidated once for the whole batch, instead of once per class as with `setClassVisibility`, and not at all when nothing changes.

This method does not redraw: when the result is not 0, call `com.benomad.msdk.mapping.MapView.redraw` on the maps that use this style.

This method must be called on the main thread (see `getPOICategories`).
